messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Building / process questions
parts:
Hi all,

Right now, our pull requests test upstream projects for our continuous integration. That means that a pull request on the Math library kicks off a test on Stan and CmdStan using those changes. A pull request on Stan kicks off a test on CmdStan.

With some of the refactoring branches, we run into issues where the upstream project needs to change with the pull request. Right now, these builds fail by design.

Questions:
- should we require a pull request on the upstream branch prior to merging?
- should we have some way of specifying the upstream job's branch? (a hacky way would be to write into some hidden text file that's removed before merging.)
- is there another way to deal with this?

An actual use case: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/1630
This causes CmdStan to fail to build due to a missing source file. It's not a hard fix, just want to know how we should handle it.


Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Building / process questions
parts:
On Tuesday, October 20, 2015 at 5:35:55 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
With some of the refactoring branches, we run into issues where the upstream project needs to change with the pull request. Right now, these builds fail by design.

Questions:
- should we require a pull request on the upstream branch prior to merging?
- should we have some way of specifying the upstream job's branch? (a hacky way would be to write into some hidden text file that's removed before merging.)
- is there another way to deal with this?

For rstan, anyone can make a pull request that both
  1. Does something with the R code or the C++ code in rstan
  2. Points the two subrepos (for Math and Lib) in StanHeaders/inst/include to any branch or commit you want

And then you should at least be able to see what happens to the Travis checks. We might not merge the pull request until we are close to releasing a new RStan, where "close" means we are ready to point the two subrepos to the develop branch of Math and Lib and presumably Math and Lib are temporarily not accepting more pull requests.


I think the same could be true of CmdStan, which would cover everything except PyStan. The rstanarm package is a slightly different matter and we need to set up a Travis configuration for it, but I don't think it is possible to break rstanarm without breaking rstan. Or at least if it were, it would be a bug in rstanarm.


Ben
